metadata.title: Education for Citizenship in Times of Global Challenge
metadata.venue: IEA International Civic and Citizenship Education Study 2022 International Report

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This ICCS 2022 report is based on a complex, multi-stage sampling design at the student and school levels, with results intended to be representative of the target grade populations within participating education systems. The report describes that the main survey collected data from about 82,000 students and 40,000 teachers across about 3,400 schools, and that results are presented with attention to whether countries met IEA technical standards for sampling, instrument preparation, field operations, scoring, and data management. The report also notes a mode-effect study and bridging samples to support fair reporting across paper-based and computer-based delivery modes, implying that scaling/equating adjustments are applied in the technical reporting pipeline. However, this excerpt does not specify the exact weight variables (e.g., student design weights) or replicate-weight procedures; therefore, analysts using the ICCS international database should follow the ICCS 2022 technical report and user guide for the correct weight and variance-estimation variables.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is an IEA international report describing the ICCS 2022 assessment framework, instruments, and descriptive/comparative results, rather than an empirical predictive modeling paper that explicitly reports how plausible values (PVs) were handled in a supervised ML pipeline. The excerpt does not provide the PV generation/combining and missing-data imputation/deletion procedures needed to classify PV handling and missing-data handling for an ML analysis. As a result, PV handling and missing-data handling are treated as not reported for this extraction because the necessary methodological details are deferred to the ICCS 2022 technical report and international database documentation.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used the ICCS 2022 main survey sample of about 82,000 students and 40,000 teachers from about 3,400 schools across participating education systems. The report indicates that comparisons over time and some reporting tables are restricted to countries that met IEA technical standards for sampling, instrument preparation, field operations, scoring, and data management; it also distinguishes results from surveys that did not meet participation requirements. Additionally, a mode-effect/bridging study included about 15,000 students from 11 countries to evaluate delivery-mode effects (paper vs computer), with adjustments intended to support fair reporting across delivery modes.

data.outcome_summary: This ICCS 2022 international report documents the assessment framework and presents descriptive and comparative findings for lower-secondary students’ civic knowledge, civic engagement, and attitudes toward civic issues, alongside contextual information from student, teacher, school, and national contexts surveys. The study collected data from about 82,000 students and 40,000 teachers across about 3,400 schools, with an option for computer-based delivery in 18 systems and paper-based delivery in 6 systems, plus a bridging/mode-effect study of about 15,000 students from 11 countries to evaluate delivery-mode impacts. The report emphasizes that results are reported with caution when countries do not meet IEA participation/technical standards, and that comparisons across ICCS cycles are limited to countries meeting those standards for all data points. Scaling/equating procedures and detailed scoring methodology are referenced as being provided in the ICCS 2022 technical report, which is where PV handling and missing-data procedures would be specified. No machine-learning predictive modeling pipeline is described in the provided excerpt, so no ML performance metrics (e.g., accuracy/AUC/RMSE) can be extracted here.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction is for an IEA/OECD-style international assessment report (ICCS 2022) rather than an empirical ML paper. The excerpt provides assessment design, instruments, and high-level reporting logic (including mode effects and participation standards) but does not specify an ML target variable, algorithms, or predictive performance metrics. Consequently, ML technique fields and structured predictive findings are intentionally left empty, and PV/missing-data handling are not classified from the excerpt because the detailed technical procedures are deferred to the ICCS 2022 technical report and database documentation.
